Subject: Post-call: RTBF & deletion workflow (FinTechCo)

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps on deletion/RTBF topics we discussed: 

1) Scope we heard on the call
   - Data types: customer PII in user profiles, transaction metadata, and model inputs (text + embeddings).
   - Usage: embeddings are derived from user-provided content for personalization; logs for debugging.

2) Redwood's standard RTBF approach (summary)
   - Primary store: records are removed from the live index within 24–72 hours of a validated delete request.
   - Backups: snapshots retained per backup policy (default 90 days). Backups are immutable snapshots — we can initiate an accelerated purge for enterprise contracts but this requires coordination with infra and legal.
   - Logs & audit trails: configurable retention (default 180 days).
   - Data residency: customer data remains in the chosen region; deletion flows operate within that region when using Redwood Private/Dedicated.

3) Constraints & notes
   - Immutable backups: if an immutable snapshot contains the record, full deletion from backups can take longer unless special purge is negotiated.
   - Legal holds/regs: if a legal hold is in place, we cannot purge until the hold is lifted.

4) Next steps
   - Lina: confirm whether embeddings derived from end-user content are in-scope and provide a list of data elements you consider PII for this request.
   - Camila/Redwood: circulate our RTBF process doc and API spec (attached) and propose timeline options (standard vs accelerated purge).
   - Schedule a technical call with our security lead (Vivek) to go over API and backup purge mechanics.

I've attached our RTBF_Process.pdf and a short RTBF_API_Spec.txt that outlines endpoints and expected request/response.

If you prefer, I can draft a short mutual action plan that captures timelines and deliverables.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RTBF_Process.pdf (summary), RTBF_API_Spec.txt (endpoints + examples)

Hi Lina — great questions, answered inline below and next steps at the end.

- Raw text vs embeddings: Redwood does not keep additional copies of raw text beyond what is required for processing; for hosted endpoints we tokenize and stream outputs but persistent storage is limited to (a) embeddings and (b) customer objects you explicitly store. We will confirm precise retention knobs with engineering, but embeddings derived by Redwood are retained per your retention policy and are removable via the RTBF API.

- Accelerated purge for backups: for Dedicated/Private customers we offer an accelerated purge option as part of enterprise contracts. Typical timelines we provide in negotiated agreements: 30–45 days for backup purge (subject to snapshot windows). Standard hosted customers default to the 90-day backup retention. We can add a clause to the contract to guarantee a 30-day backup purge for your Dedicated commitment.

- Deletion event logs: yes — we emit a deletion event per record with a timestamp and request id. We can provide an export of those events for auditor review.

- SOC2 evidence: I will attach a SOC2 artifact and our security questionnaire responses via a secure share (link below). For now, the RTBF_Process.pdf includes the high-level controls.

Next steps (proposed):
  1) Lina: send a short list of PII elements and confirm embeddings are in-scope (reply to this thread).
  2) Camila: set up a technical call with Vivek and your devops team to walk API flows and backup purge options — propose Tue/Thu availability next week.
  3) Camila/Legal: prepare proposed contract language for accelerated backup purge (30-day SLA) and share initial draft.

Link to secure share: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fintechco-rtbf

Thanks!
Camila

Looping in a few technical details we should be ready to discuss on the call with FinTechCo:

- API details: RTBF endpoint is POST /v1/admin/deletions with payload: {customer_id, record_ids[], reason, request_id}. Response includes deletion_job_id and estimated completion timestamp. (See attached RTBF_API_Spec.txt for examples.)
- Backups: snapshots are taken daily at 02:00 UTC; accelerated purge requires identifying affected snapshot(s) and running an index rebuild which is I/O intensive — typical target for enterprise accelerated purge is 30–45 days depending on snapshot alignment.
- Logs/audit: we emit deletion events to the audit log stream; we can provide a signed export for compliance.
- Edge cases: if FinTechCo stores PII only in customer-managed feature stores and only sends ephemeral inputs to Redwood, scope narrows to request/response logs and we can tailor retention accordingly.

Action items for the call:
 - Camila: get list of PII elements and a sample record id mapping (hashes are fine).
 - FinTechCo: confirm whether legal holds apply to the data sets in scope.
 - Infra: be prepared to estimate cost/impact for accelerated purge (compute + reindex windows).

-Vivek
Director of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
